cells.tense: You are choosing your direction here, with the pen actually in your hand.
cells.act: hold your shape under the weight
cells.ask: When the next weight lands this week, don't brace against it or bend under it. Hold your shape a minute longer than you usually would, and notice what stays standing.
cells.core:
You can say this, not that, and mean it. Where something is ending here, you're not talking about it from a distance — you're in it, deciding what stays and what goes, and it comes from seeing clearly instead of from something pushing you. There's a direction in your life right now that you're holding with a steady hand.

The part that's free to grow next is endurance — not gritted teeth, just the ability to bear weight without letting it crush you or harden you. You've been carrying this; you can also hold it at the size it actually is. So when the next weight lands, don't brace or bend. Hold your shape a minute longer than usual, and watch what stays standing.

cells.tense: You are bracing against a future you keep trying to write in advance.
cells.act: see the whole pattern you are standing inside
cells.ask: Before you push the ending to happen on your schedule, stop and look at the whole shape of it — what's already moving, what you're steering, what you're forcing. See the pattern, and don't touch it yet.
cells.core:
Somewhere in this ending, you've stopped steering and started forcing. It looks like direction, but your hands are tight on it — pushing the outcome to arrive on a schedule you've set, managing how it lands, gripping the parts that won't move yet. The pressure isn't coming from the ending; it's coming from how far ahead you're standing.

What brings you back is seeing the whole pattern instead of the next move. Before you force anything this week, stop and look at the whole shape — what's already moving, what you're actually steering, what you're pushing uphill. See it and set it down for now. That kind of seeing keeps deepening, and it's what puts the pen back in the present.

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door that closed behind you a while back.
cells.act: do the thing in your own way, without proving it
cells.ask: Pick one ordinary task you'd normally do the expected way. Do it your way instead, once, and don't explain it to anyone. No announcement, no defense — just that one task, done as only you do it.
cells.core:
The ending here has already happened, and part of you is still waiting for it to unhappen. The direction you used to have — say this, not that — has gone quiet, and what's left is a shrug: what's the point. It isn't gone. It's starved, and pushing harder at what already ended won't bring it back.

It comes back by doing one ordinary task the way you'd naturally do it, without proving it to anyone. Pick something small, do it your way, and skip the explanation. Not a performance, not a statement. Just you, doing it as only you would, for a minute. That's the small charge that gets the current moving again.

cells.tense: You are steering without noticing your hand is the one on the wheel.
cells.act: put your own name on what is already yours
cells.ask: Find one thing around you that you set in motion yourself — small or old, doesn't matter — and say, on paper or plainly, that you did it. Not as a boast. Just put your name back on it.
cells.core:
You're directing things here, and your account of it has you along for the ride. Things are ending around you the way seasons end, or so it reads from inside — but the endings keep landing near choices you made, and the momentum you call circumstance has your fingerprints on it. Habit has been writing in a room where you hold the pen.

What returns first is the simplest part of you: the thing you actually are, showing without needing to prove it. Find one thing near you that you set in motion — small, or old enough that nobody mentions it now — and say plainly that you did it. Not a boast; just your name back on what was already yours.
